title: Normalized ramified scalar and adjunction preparation
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite-field datum D of characteristic p different from l, finite extensions E and L of Q_l and an embedding i:E→L. Let f:X→Y be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type D.k-schemes, with a fixed compactification c. Fix a ramification index e≥1 with pi_E O_L=pi_L^e O_L. Use the strict coefficient-system and integral constructible categories and the specified support, scalar, and reduction functors of [def-coef-finite-scalar-mate-data]. There exist simultaneous Context data a for these actual functors such that the specified proper/open system scalar comparison a.alpha is invertible, and the following preparation data exist: finite scalar tensor preserves the finite domains on X and Y, with natural evaluation isomorphisms and actual quotient-transition equations at retained indices e(n+1); the integral and system adjunctions have compatible left/right evaluation isomorphisms satisfying both unit and counit laws; the actual completion unit is invertible on all four integral constructible categories; the scalar-reduction isomorphisms on X and Y are the actual scalar-model/reduction counits; retained and full limits have cofinal natural isomorphisms with the stated two-coordinate Roos normalization; the support evaluation maps have the inverse-completion-unit normalization; and both the reduction of M and its exceptional system have common finite Tor intervals for every integral constructible M on Y. This preparation asserts none of the five limit-realization isomorphisms of the parent and no support-comparison limit square. From it the five isomorphisms are defined by explicit compositions of its cofinal maps, inverse adjunction comparisons, scalar-model inverses, support realizations and completion units.

proof.text: Choose a cohomological interval $[a,b]$ for the first reduction of $M$. The residue-Tor theorem gives this same Tor interval for every level of $N$. The integral exceptional theorem gives $P=G_RM\in\mathcal C_R(X)$ and the interval $[a-2d_X,b+2d_Y]$ for its reductions, using dimension bounds $0$ on empty schemes. By its specified construction $P=\mathcal L_{R,X}\mathsf E_RN$. Effectivity identifies the actual counit $\mathcal R_{R,X}P\to\mathsf E_RN$ with an isomorphism: its evaluations are precisely the canonical projection-adjoint comparisons. Thus $\mathsf E_RN$ has that uniform Tor interval, rather than merely levelwise finite Tor dimension.

proof.text: For every $K\in\mathcal C_R(W)$, integral scalar-extension constructibility gives $T_WK\in\mathcal C_S(W)$. The finite-free completed-scalar comparison identifies its ordinary tensor presentation with the specified strict quotient-limit presentation by $\chi_K$. At every full $S$-level $m$, choose $n$ with $en\ge m$; its reduction is $K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}S/v^m$. The scalar Tor-bound theorem shows that a uniform interval for the $K_n$ remains an interval at every such $m$. Apply this to $M$ and $P=G_RM$. This checks the domains of $G_S$ and $F_S$ used below, including the intermediate levels outside $en$.

source.place: Finite scalar extension paragraph: finite free tensor and the derived limit defining integral compact support; expanded using actual reduction/limit counits.

proof.text:
We first specify the common scalar-reduction identification, for any $K\in\mathcal C_R(W)$. On a flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to K$, the retained reductions of ordinary scalar extension are
$$(Q\otimes_{\widehat R_W}\widehat S_W)\otimes_{\widehat S_W}(B_n)_W=(Q\otimes_{\widehat R_W}(A_n)_W)\otimes_{(A_n)_W}(B_n)_W.$$
K-flat change of rings makes both sides representatives of the indicated derived reductions. The reassociation sends $(x\otimes s)\otimes b$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes\bar s b$; its inverse sends $(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes ab$. They commute with every quotient on these complexes and with chain maps. They therefore identify $\mathcal R_{S,W}^{(e)}T_WK$ with $\mathsf T_W^{(e)}\mathcal R_{R,W}K$ as functors, using $\chi_K$ for the ordinary presentation. Apply the canonical arithmetic restriction isomorphism to the full reduction tower. It preserves the unit cone and satisfies $p_n\rho_e=p_{en}$; completeness and the reduction/limit unit consequently give
$$\mathcal L_{S,W}^{(e)}\mathsf T_W^{(e)}\mathcal R_{R,W}K\cong T_WK.$$
These maps use the actual quotient cone, so their projection-adjoints are the actual reduction counits.

proof.text: Choose simultaneous system and integral adjunctions and identify them through the genuine reduction/limit counits. Normalize support evaluation by its fixed limit realization and the completion unit. The triangles give both unit/counit evaluation equations and the support normalization. No exceptional or support limit identification is assumed. The strict finite-free proper/open comparison is invertible by the same reduced integral basis and finite-sum distributivity before evaluation.
